articles.title: Samsung & SK hynix Have Set A Dangerous Greed Cycle That Has Trickled Down To Suppliers Like ASML, Who Now Want To Match Their Customers’ Profit Margins - Wccftech
articles.summary: Samsung & SK hynix Have Set A Dangerous Greed Cycle That Has Trickled Down To Suppliers Like ASML, Who Now Want To Match Their Customers’ Profit Margins  Wccftech
articles.full_text:
The profits being raked in by Samsung and SK hynix during the DRAM shortage have made both memory manufacturers the source of envy amongst high-profile suppliers like ASML, which is now reportedly seeking a price hike to match what its clients are generating in annual net earnings. According to the latest report, the changes have been finalized, setting a perilous precedent across the entire industry.
ASML is reportedly charging a flat 10 percent higher fee for every EUV and DUV part, with Samsung and SK hynix seemingly having agreed
The Dutch equipment manufacturer is raising prices for all replacement parts found in its machines. According to The Elec, these changes are expected to take effect in January 2027, with the proposal reportedly sent to both Samsung and SK hynix through their Korean subsidiaries last month. Given the scale at which both manufacturers are generating profits, they likely felt that a 10 percent price hike was a drop in the bucket, so based on the fresh details, they agreed.
Both EUV and DUV equipment have a plethora of moving parts that are susceptible to wear and tear over time. These parts include photolithography equipment, optical paraphernalia such as lenses, mirrors, light sources, and precision actuators. With every single one of these parts obtaining a 10 percent price hike, it’s clear that, being the only manufacturer of advanced EUV machinery, ASML doesn’t wish to get left behind during the AI boom and wants the same opportunity as Samsung and SK hynix when it comes to printing money.
In fact, one unnamed industry source has noted that while prices have risen across an entire spectrum of components, ASML seeks a larger margin to match what its customers, Samsung and SK hynix, are making. The Dutch firm has forecasted that its revenue would increase by more than 30 percent this year, and that’s without the price hike initiated. Additionally, Chinese customers who intend to purchase DUV equipment will also have to pay an additional 10 percent.
Given that the entire industry wants an upper hand in the AI race, these clients have agreed to the hike. While ASML is part of the industry responsible for mass-producing cutting-edge wafers, it hasn’t been adversely impacted by memory and NAND flash shortages, so it’s clear the company wants to capitalize in the same way as Samsung and SK hynix. Unfortunately, this practice has set off a chain reaction spreading through the entire industry.
Companies like Applied Materials and Japan’s Tokyo Electron have increased the price of their products, and with this cycle seeing no end, consumers are going to receive the short end of the stick.
News Source: The Elec

articles.title: [不同来源] One with the world? A new look at brains transformed by psychedelics.
articles.summary: Participants meditated inside an MRI tube, with and without psilocybin.
articles.full_text:
For about a decade, the mainstream understanding has been that psychedelics cause chaos in the brain. Brain networks—the stable patterns of communication that handle vision, attention, or our sense of self, and more—loosen and start talking to each other all at once. EEG traces get noisier and more complex. “Think of the networks of the brain as highways,” says Devon Stoliker, a neuroscientist at Monash University. “Under psychedelics, these highways break down into many different directions.”
In a recent Nature study, Stoliker’s team designed an experiment to test whether these directions are truly chaotic and random. Researchers gathered 62 people who had never taken a psychedelic before, gave them 19 milligrams of psilocybin, a common psychedelic found in certain fungi, and scanned their brains. Then, they used AI to analyze the drugged and sober brain scans. What emerged was not exactly chaos.
An uninterrupted trip
Stoliker thinks chaos is not a satisfactory explanation for psychedelics’ effect on the brain. “It never really explained why an individual would have a meaningful experience, why they might have insight, why they might experience clarity, and why these might translate into positive psychological changes,” Stoliker says. To investigate if there are other explanations, he and his colleagues designed a study called PsiConnect.Read full article

articles.full_text:
I remember hearing a while ago that Dwarf Fortress didn't use version control. That fact has been lodged in my head, because given its inherent complexity I have trouble imagining a codebase that would benefit from version control more. That's art.
I went looking and I'm sad to report that the days without version control appear to have ended. Quoting Tarn Adams over time:

March 2013: "I don't use version control -- I didn't like the feeling of having the code get committed into a black box thingy with no immediate upside"
March 2016: "I don’t even use version control. If you don’t know what that is then you’re not gonna yell at me. If you even know what version control is you’re gonna be like, ‘You don’t use version control? You don’t use source control? What is wrong with you? How can you even work? I’m just not cut out for it, in a sense. It’s been 15 years, so the reasons have change over time, but that’s my current understanding of it." 
March 2023: "I've got Discord channels to check and version control stuff to use now, so the process is definitely a little more involved"

That March 2023 quote comes from an interview about the release on Steam which made them millionaires. I'm a tiny bit sad that they gave in before they hit that milestone, but what an impressive run.

    Tags: version-control
